text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING - us-west-2 runtime-serving latency tail increase detected after canary deploy (release/2026-03-16T20:12). Symptoms: p99 spikes to 5-12s, throughput down ~30%. Triggering oncall.

eva: I'm paged, taking lead. I'll spin up the bridge. Quick context: this was a canary that changed batching window + kernel selector heuristic.

sahil: I'm on logs. Early find: kernel_fallback spikes on canary hosts and microbatch size collapsing to 1. Running quick grep: `kubectl logs -l role=runtime-canary -n runtime | grep kernel_fallback`

rico: KV cache miss rate is up on the same hosts, seeing a lot of cache invalidations. Looks like prefetch misalignment + increased eviction. Customer impact: Dedicated pools for a few customers seeing elevated p99 and some 503s.

eva: Mitigation plan: 1) Pause canary traffic (feature flag flip). 2) Route traffic to stable pool. 3) If no improvement, rollback canary revision. Who can flip the flag? @jen

jen: I flipped `canary_cutover=false` via console — traffic percentage dropped from 10% -> 0% within ~60s. Confirmed change: cfg_hash=v2->v1.

sahil: After the flag flip p99 dropped from ~9s -> ~3s but throughput still not fully recovered. Kernel_fallback logs show allocator pressure on nodes; seems some canary kernel variants forced fallback and caused cross-node pressure even on stable pods due to shared node resources.

rico: I'm draining the worst nodes now: `orchctl drain node-az3-xy-12` for three affected nodes. That should stop the noisy eviction cycles and free KV cache pressure.

incident-bot: Conference bridge created: https://meet.internal/bridges/INC-6701 (oncall + eng-runtime + ops)

eva: @sahil can you check batching windows? If canary has a much shorter window it could create microbatch churn and force the slow kernel path.

sahil: Confirmed — canary hosts had `batching.window_ms=12` vs stable `40ms`. That mismatch makes microbatches tiny and increases per-request overhead and kernel selector chooses the safe but slower kernels. Reverting canary config to 40ms now.

jen: Config rollback applied and validated (cfg_hash back to v1). Watching metrics.

sahil: p50 back to normal, p99 trending down to ~700ms. Throughput recovering to ~95% of baseline after config revert and node drains. No new 5xx errors in the last 4 minutes.

eva: Good containment. Next steps: keep canary paused, open an incident ticket with timeline and assign postmortem. Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous kernel selector tweak + batching window regression + node memory pressure leading to kernel fallbacks and KV thrash.

rico: I'll open a backlog task for CS to reconcile delayed requests for affected tenants (noting Acme Analytics and Finex).

jen: Created INC-6701, assigned postmortem owner to me. Labels: sev2, release, rollback. I'll schedule the RCA meeting tomorrow.

sahil: Uploaded logs + grep snippets to runbook gist: https://gists.internal/6701-logs. Also adding a temporary alert for `kernel_fallback.count > 5/min` in canary namespace.

eva: Action items captured: (1) Add config validation step in rollout pipeline to prevent batching mismatch, (2) Add node-isolation policy for canaries, (3) Add kernel_fallback metric alert and automation to cut canary traffic automatically.

jen: Notifying CS & account owners now, will include timeline and interim mitigation notes.

eva: Thanks team. Closing the oncall paging after 30m stable window unless someone sees regressions. Please append any additional notes to INC-6701. :thumbsup:
